source: NCERT Class XI, Performing Arts & Cultural Heritage of India, Ch. 6 (Puppetry and Martial Art Traditions).

sections.heading: 1. Puppetry — Types
points: Indian **puppetry** is an ancient folk art telling stories from epics and legends; four main types:

sub: **String puppets (marionettes)** — e.g. **Kathputli (Rajasthan)**, Kundhei (Odisha), Gombeyatta (Karnataka), Bommalattam (Tamil Nadu).
**Shadow puppets** — flat leather figures against a lit screen — e.g. **Tholu Bommalata (Andhra)**, Togalu Gombeyatta (Karnataka), Ravanachhaya (Odisha).

sections.heading: 2. Significance of Puppetry
points: Puppetry combines **storytelling, music, dance and craft**; used for entertainment and moral/social education.
It preserves regional themes (Ramayana, Mahabharata, folk tales).
A dying folk art now being revived.

sections.heading: 3. Martial Art Traditions
points: India has many traditional **martial arts**, often linked with dance and ritual:

sub: **Kalaripayattu (Kerala)** — one of the oldest martial arts in the world.

sections.heading: 4. Cultural Value
points: Martial arts blend **physical skill, discipline, and often spiritual/ritual** dimensions.
Many are tied to festivals and community identity (e.g. Gatka at Sikh events).
Efforts are on to **preserve and promote** these traditions.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Four puppet types: string (Kathputli-Rajasthan), shadow (Tholu Bommalata-AP), rod (Putul Nautch-Bengal), glove (Pavakoothu-Kerala).
Kalaripayattu (Kerala) = one of the oldest martial arts.
Silambam = Tamil Nadu (staff); Gatka = Punjab (Sikh sword).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Kalaripayattu = Kerala** (among the world's oldest martial arts).
**Shadow puppets** use flat leather figures against a **lit screen**.
